title: Variance-aware percentile targets and throttle-circuit for Dedicated Fleet Autoscaler
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Goal: Implement an autoscaling policy extension for Dedicated fleets that (1) targets percentile-based throughput/latency objectives using variance-aware smoothing, and (2) introduces a throttle-circuit (temporary scaling inhibitor) to avoid oscillation during high-variance demand spikes. This ticket covers design, core algorithm changes, integration tests, and a staged rollout.

Context: Our existing autoscaler targets single-point metrics (e.g., target RPS per-GPU) and uses moving averages for smoothing. This approach reacts poorly to highly bursty tenant workloads: we either over-provision on transient spikes (cost) or oscillate (instability and degraded SLOs). We also lack a short-duration inhibition mechanism that can avoid thrashing when predictions/forecasts are uncertain.

Scope: 1) Add a new target type: variance-aware percentile (configurable percentile, e.g., p90/p95) computed from short-window sliding windows with exponential decay. 2) Implement a confidence signal derived from observed variance and request churn; when confidence is low, apply conservative slew rates and activate the throttle-circuit. 3) Expose policy knobs in Dedicated config (percentile, window_size_sec, variance_threshold, throttle_duration_sec, min_slew, max_surge). 4) Add integration tests, canary rollout plan, dashboards, and cost/regression checks.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler supports new policy field 'target_type: percentile_variance_aware' and accepts percentile and window config.
Percentile estimates are computed server-side with bounded memory and CPU overhead (benchmarks <5% CPU increase on autoscaler control plane nodes).
Throttle-circuit activates when variance_threshold exceeded and prevents further scale-ups for throttle_duration_sec, but allows scale-downs per safety policy.

End-to-end simulation: synthetic burst workload (50x RPS for 15s every 2 minutes) yields a reduction in scale oscillations >= 40% versus baseline (moving-average target) while keeping p95 latency below SLO 99% of time.
Configurable rollout: feature flag + per-tenant opt-in with telemetry emitted (policy_active, throttle_triggered_count, percentile_value, confidence_score).
Operational dashboards and alerting for: repeated throttle triggers, long-lasting underprovisioning (p95 > SLO for >5m), and unexpected cost delta >10% for a tenant after enabling the policy.
discussion: 2026-02-20 Sofia R.: Kickoff — initial design sketch attached. We should avoid heavy tail quantile algorithms; prefer digest-like bounded estimators. Linking design doc in design_links.

2026-02-25 Owen P.: Prototype percentiles using t-digest on the control plane. Memory looks fine; need to instrument CPU. Also observed that raw percentile swings on tiny windows cause throttle to trigger too often — added exponential decay and min-sample constraints.

2026-02-28 Casey Lin (SRE): Recommend allowing scale-downs while throttle is active to clear pressure fast; otherwise latency risk increases. Added as design note — throttle only blocks scale-ups, not scale-downs.
2026-03-04 Priya Kapoor (Product): For Dedicated customers with strict throughput guarantees, default to p95 with conservative variance_threshold; expose per-tenant overrides.
2026-03-08 QA: Integration test harness added that replays recorded tenant traces. Observed 45% fewer churned scaling steps under bursty traces. Need longer-run soak to check cost impact.
2026-03-12 Owen P.: Implemented throttle-circuit prototype (PR linked). Ready for internal canary on non-critical tenants next week.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/2124 - prototype t-digest percentile estimator and policy flags
experiments: Synthetic spike replay (trace set: dedicated-bursty-2025-12) — baseline oscillations: median 12 scaling events/hour; new policy: median 7 scaling events/hour.
Cost delta measured in lab: +3% steady-state for p95 targeting vs baseline moving-average, but 18% reduced transient over-provision during spikes (net savings dependent on workload pattern).
Control-plane CPU impact: +3.8% on autoscaler replicas under heavy tenant counts (scaled to 2000 tenants).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): deploy feature-flagged autoscaler to internal staging; run replay tests (done).
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 non-critical Dedicated tenants for 48h; monitor throttle-triggered_count and p95 tail (SRE + oncall watch).
Phase 2 (gradual): ramp to 25% of new Dedicated tenants over 2 weeks; auto-disable on alerted regressions (playbook attached).
Phase 3 (opt-in GA): allow tenant admins to opt in via Console for new Dedicated fleets, then later offer as default with conservative params.
Rollback criteria: sustained p95 > SLO for 10m, throttle-trigger_count > X in 1h, or cost delta > 10% sustained for 24h.
monitoring: Telemetry emitted: autoscaler.policy.percentile_value, autoscaler.policy.confidence_score, autoscaler.policy.throttle_active (0/1), throttle_triggered_count
Dashboards: per-tenant timeseries for p50/p90/p95/p99 throughput and latency, scaling event count, headroom credits, and control-plane CPU.
Alerts: p95_slo_breach (>=2m above SLO), throttle_flood (throttle_triggered_count > 10 in 1h), unexpected_cost_delta (>10% over 24h).
risks: Over-conservatism: overly aggressive throttle could under-provision during real sustained demand, causing SLO violations. Mitigation: allow manual override and default conservative parameters; allow immediate scale-ups if queue/backpressure metrics exceed hard thresholds.
Estimator instability: percentile estimators on small sample sizes may be noisy. Mitigation: min_sample and exponential decay smoothing; confidence score gating.
Cost regression for workloads that are spiky but valuable (higher latency acceptable). Mitigation: per-tenant opt-out and cost-impact telemetry before enabling by default.
